paragraphs.text: Origen holdeth Solomon to have been penman of all these songs of degrees, as hath been before noted. But as that is not likely (see the titles of Psa 122:1; Psa 124:1; Psa 131:1), so divers interpreters conceive this to be his; because much of it is the same with that prayer he made at the dedication of the temple, 2Ch 6:16; 2Ch 6:14; 2Ch 6:42. Here, then, he prayeth God to remember David, that is (not his merits and suffrages, as the monks would have it, but), the promises made unto him (for the which Solomon praised God as well as for the performance to himself, 2Ch 6:10), and his singular solicitude about the house and worship of God, which was so great, as that it affected, yea, afflicted his spirit; whence it followeth here, "and all his afflictions"; for which it is, 2Ch 6:42, the mercies or kindness of David, Ita ut dormire non potuerit (Kimchi.)
paragraphs.anchor: Lord, remember David

paragraphs.text: Out of the abundance of his affections, 1Ch 29:3, {see Psa 119:106} he solemnly took God to witness; and this he did, say the Rabbis, at that time when he saw the punishing angel, and was terrified.
paragraphs.anchor: How he sware unto the Lord

paragraphs.text: Jacob is mentioned, say the Hebrews, Quia primo vovit. because he first vowed to God, Gen 28:20, whence he is called, Pater votorum, the Father of vows (Kimchi, Aben Ezra).
paragraphs.anchor: And vowed unto the mighty God of Jacob

paragraphs.text: i.e. Of my newly built house, 1Ch 15:1 2Sa 1:2. Those in Malachi were not so well minded, Psa 1:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely I will not come into the tabernacle of my house

paragraphs.text: viz. With any good content; or, more than needs must.
paragraphs.anchor: I will not give sleep to mine eyes

paragraphs.text: The Jewish doctors tell us, that as the earth is in the middle of the world, so is Judea in the middle of the earth, Jerusalem in the middle of Judea, the temple in the middle of Jerusalem, and the ark in the middle of the temple.
paragraphs.anchor: Until I find out a place for the Lord

paragraphs.text: Heb. habitations; haply because the temple consisted of three parts, or partitions.
paragraphs.anchor: An habitation

paragraphs.text: At Bethlehem Ephratah, David’s birth place, there we heard of it long since by our progenitors. "Of it," that is, of the ark, saith Chrysostom; of God’s resting place, saith Austin; of the place where Christ should be born, saith Jerome; where the temple should be set, saith Aben Ezra; where the Shechinah, or Divine presence should reside, say other Rabbis, Dicit eam in foemin, i.e. diviuam praesentiam (R. Arama).
paragraphs.anchor: Lo, we heard of it at Ephratah

paragraphs.text: At Jerusalem, say some; or at Kirjathjearim, as others will have it. The Chaldee interpreteth it of the wood of Libanus; the place, saith he, where the patriarchs worshipped.
paragraphs.anchor: We found it in the fields of the wood

paragraphs.text: We will cheerfully and unanimously frequent his public worship, in the place he hath pitched upon (called his gates, and his courts, Psa 100:4), saying as Psa 132:8-10: επου τω θεω, follow God, was the rule among the very heathens.
paragraphs.anchor: We will go into his tabernacles

paragraphs.text: i.e. At his ark, where he uttered oracles and wrought miracles, &c., which yet was but his footstool, to lift his people heavenward, Christward, who was the truth of that type, the ark, the mercy seat.
paragraphs.anchor: We will worship at his footstool

paragraphs.text: The place of thy rest; for the ark was transportative till settled in Solomon’s temple; so, till we come to heaven, we are in continual motion.
paragraphs.anchor: Arise, O Lord, into thy rest

paragraphs.text: The ark in the temple was the chiefest evidence of God’s presence, and the most principal type of Christ, in whom the fulness of the Godhead dwelleth bodily. The word is aron, which is put for a coffin, coffer, or chest, Gen 50:26 2Ki 12:9. This showeth, that all the counsels of God, all the love and favour of God, all that God accounteth precious, are treasured up in Christ, Col 2:3; Col 1:13 Isa 42:1 Heb 10:12.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou, and the ark of thy strength

paragraphs.text: i.e. With salvation, as Psa 132:16. No surer sign of God’s gracious presence with a people, than a powerful ministry, clothed with inward purity and holiness, represented by the holy garments.
paragraphs.anchor: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness

paragraphs.text: i.e. Those that are converted by such a ministry, let those that are justified by faith have peace with God, and joy unspeakable, full of glory.
paragraphs.anchor: And let thy saints shout for joy

paragraphs.text: For thy servant David’s sake] For thy covenant’s sake made with him, and for thy Christ’s sake, who is oft called David, as Hos 3:5, so for the Lord’s sake, Dan 9:17.
Of thy Christ; defer not his coming, or deny not my request, as 1Ki 2:16-17; 1Ki 2:20.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn not away the face of thine anointed

paragraphs.text: The eternity of Israel cannot lie, 1Sa 15:29, yet tendering our infirmity, he sweareth and sealeth to us.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord hath sworn in truth

paragraphs.text: David was excellent at making the utmost of a promise, at pressing and oppressing it, till he had expressed the sweetness out of it, Isa 66:11. See how he improveth God’s promise, and worketh upon it, 1Ch 17:23-26. Solomon had learned to do the like.
paragraphs.anchor: Of the fruit of thy body

paragraphs.text: Although God’s covenant is free, yet it is delivered under certain conditions on our part to be observed; which are as an oar in a boat, or stern in a ship, turning it this way or that, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: If thy children will keep my covenant

paragraphs.text: For a long season; and Christ, for all eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: For evermore

paragraphs.text: He chose it for his love; and loved it for his choice.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath chosen Zion

paragraphs.text: It was so because God was pleased to make it so; he rested in his love; he would seek no farther, Zep 3:17.
paragraphs.anchor: This is my rest for ever

paragraphs.text: This alone made the difference, as it also did between Aaron’s rod and the rest that were laid with it.
paragraphs.anchor: For I have desired it

paragraphs.text: Her stock and her store; so that she shall not want necessaries, which yet she shall hunt for (that is, labour for), as the Hebrew word importeth; and know how she comes by; Viatico eius affatim benedicam (Trem.): therefore it is added,
paragraphs.anchor: I will abundantly bless her provision

paragraphs.text: Dainties I will not promise them; a sufficiency, but not a superfluity; poor they may be, but not destitute; bread they shall have, and of that, God’s plenty, as they say; enough to bring them to their Father’s house, where is bread enough. Let not, therefore, the poor Israelite fear to bring his offerings, or to disfurnish himself for God’s worship, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: I will satisfy her poor with bread

paragraphs.text: So that they shall save themselves and those that hear them, 1Ti 4:16. Thus God answereth his people’s prayers both for temporals and spirituals; see Psa 132:9, and that with an overplus of comfort; they shall shout aloud.
paragraphs.anchor: I will also clothe her priests, &c.

paragraphs.text: A metaphor from those living creatures, quorum ramosa sunt cornua, which have snags in their heads (as deer have), which are unto them instead of boughs. For "horn," some read beam of David. Confer Luk 1:78.
paragraphs.anchor: There will I make the horn of David to bud

paragraphs.text: i.e. A successor ( - cui lampada tradat), and that a glorious one at length, Christ, who is αυτοφως, light essential, Joh 12:46. Of Ascanius the son of Aeneas, and likewise of Tullus Hostilius, it is reported, that light flames were seen about their heads when they lay in their cradles; and that thereby was foresignified that they should be kings.
paragraphs.anchor: I have ordained a lamp

paragraphs.text: Shame shall be the promotion of all such fools as set against Christ and his people; yea, they shall be clothed with it; so that it shall be conspicuous to all men.
paragraphs.anchor: His enemies will I clothe with shame

paragraphs.text: His royal diadem, whereby he is separated (Nezer) and distinguished from other men. Alexander dropped his diadem once into the water, and because he who fetched it out, put it on his own head while he swam out with it, he cut off his head. Our Edward IV hanged one for saying he would make his son owner of the crown; though he only meant his own house (having a crown for the sign) in Cheapside.
paragraphs.anchor: But upon himself shall his crown flourish
